name: Boundary Creeper with Drop-7 Quarter Coverage Shell
coverage: Drop 7 — Cover 3 Match with Simulated Edge Creeper

summary.motive: Drop 7 defenders into multi-layered zone coverage by disguising a pass rusher as a creeper, then rushing only 3 linemen while flooding all throwing windows.
summary.keyDefender: Left OLB Creeper (Pre-snap Rush Alignment, Post-snap Drop)
summary.whyItWorks: The LOLB creeper fools the QB's hot-read expectations — the QB expects a 5-man pressure but gets only 3 rushers and 7 coverage defenders. Every intermediate route is bracketed by quarters match rules, leaving only a short check-down under the first-down marker.
summary.failureMode: A mobile QB who scrambles away from the pocket, or a TE on a crossing route that forces the MIKE linebacker out of position before the FS can provide over-the-top help.

beats.title: 1. LOLB Creeper Disguise
beats.text: The left outside linebacker aligns in a two-point pass rush stance on the boundary edge, baiting the offensive tackle into a set position. At the snap, he drops into flat zone coverage — creating an extra dropper that confuses the QB's hot-read system.

beats.title: 2. 3-Man Rush, 7-Man Drop
beats.text: Only three linemen rush (4iL, NOSE, 4iR) while 7 defenders drop into deep coverage zones. The defense sacrifices immediate pressure for a coverage umbrella that has no throwing windows anywhere on the field.

beats.title: 3. TE Cross Split Zone Read
beats.text: The TE attempts to split the MIKE and STAR zones on a 10-yard cross. Shula's quarters shell activates zone replacement rules — MIKE sinks with TE, FS rotates over-the-top as a second layer of help, and STAR holds H's hook in quarters match.

beats.title: 4. QB Pressured, Check-Down
beats.text: With 7 defenders in coverage and all primary targets bracketed or covered, the QB is flushed from the pocket. The only outlet is a short RB check-down — Shula's Drop-7 design forces exactly this outcome: a minimal gain on 3rd-and-7.

relations.tell: LOLB walks up to line in edge rush stance before snap — this is the creeper tell; if he drops, expect a 3-man rush with 7 in coverage.
